title: Slow Cooker Chicken Adobo

items: 2½–3 lb bone-in skin-on chicken thighs (or thighs and drumsticks), fully thawed
½ cup vinegar (Filipino cane vinegar, white vinegar or apple cider vinegar)
1 tsp whole black peppercorns, lightly crushed

steps: Pat the chicken dry. Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat and cook the thighs skin side down 5–6 min, until golden.
Set the chicken in the slow cooker skin side up. Stir together the soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay leaves, peppercorns, brown sugar and water, and pour it over the chicken.
Cover and cook on low 4–5 hr, until the thickest thigh reads at least 175°F and is tender but not falling apart.
Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches from the heat. Line a rimmed sheet pan with foil, set the thighs on it skin side up, and broil 3–5 min, until the skin crisps.
Skim the fat from the cooking liquid and pour it into a medium saucepan. Simmer over medium heat 8–10 min, until reduced by about half and slightly syrupy. Remove the bay leaves.
Serve the chicken over rice with the sauce spooned over it, and top with green onions.
tips: For more flavor, marinate the chicken in the sauce in a zip-top bag in the fridge 1–8 hr. Pat it dry before browning and use the marinade as the sauce.
Too sour? Simmer the sauce a few minutes longer and add a little more sugar. Too salty? Thin it with water, and use low-sodium soy next time.
Leftovers make great adobo fried rice: chop the meat and stir-fry it with day-old rice, garlic and a spoonful of the sauce.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days; adobo tastes even better on day 2. Freezer up to 3 months in the sauce. Reheat covered over medium-low heat until it reaches 165°F.
